solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Spooner’s polite request to sing for tropical forest native

indicators.note: Reverend Spooner famously swapped the opening sounds of neighbouring words, so his version of a phrase trades its initial sounds

blocks.note: the word that makes a request polite
to chant is to sing in unison
swapping the opening PL and CH sounds of the two words

explanation.surface: Someone politely asks an islander from the rainforest to give them a song.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Native' suggests a person, but it is a plant: the Swiss cheese plant or Monstera, a familiar houseplant that grows wild in rainforest.
explanation.definitionFit: The Swiss cheese plant, Monstera, grows wild in the rainforests of Central America before becoming a popular houseplant.

clue.text: Mount electrical item

blocks.note: first meaning: a horse ridden into battle
second meaning: a device that refills a battery

explanation.walkthrough: 'Mount' looks like a verb, as in mounting a socket on a wall, but it is a noun: an animal you ride.
explanation.definitionFit: A knight's warhorse is called this, and so is the plug-in gadget that tops up a phone battery.

clue.text: Top of tree moving down, leaves are found

indicators.note: the top of a word in a down entry is its first letter
a letter that moves down a column quits its place and drops to the bottom of the entry

blocks.note: leaves is used as a verb: goes out
first letter of tree

explanation.surface: Autumn: the crown of a tree sheds downward and fallen leaves lie everywhere.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leaves' looks like foliage but is the verb EXITS; its T slides from the middle to the bottom of the down entry, giving EXIST.
explanation.definitionFit: To exist is to be present or occur somewhere, which is what things that are found do.

clue.text: Switching sides, fastens bag

indicators.note: the sides of a word are its two end letters, and switching them puts each where the other was

blocks.note: to latch is to fasten a door or gate

explanation.surface: Someone changes a bag strap over to the other shoulder and does up the clasp.
explanation.walkthrough: Swap the first and last letters of LATCHES, L and S, and SATCHEL appears.
explanation.definitionFit: A satchel is a shoulder bag with a flap, traditionally carried by schoolchildren for their books.

clue.text: Lager beginning to pour over trays

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its opening letter
turning something over flips it, so the letters run the other way

blocks.note: first letter of pour
Stella Artois is a well-known brand of Belgian lager

explanation.surface: A barman starts pouring a lager over a stack of drinks trays.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lager' is a brand, Stella, which turned over and placed below P gives PALLETS; in a down entry 'over' also places the P on top.
explanation.definitionFit: Pallets are flat wooden platforms on which goods are stacked and moved by forklift, a kind of large tray.

clue.text: One declining tricky brainteaser I’m hesitant to ignore

indicators.note: what is ignored is left out, so those letters are dropped
something tricky is twisted or devious, so the letters get twisted into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
the sound a hesitant speaker makes

explanation.surface: A puzzler hesitates over a hard brainteaser and turns it down.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove ER, the hesitant noise, from BRAINTEASER, then rearrange the remaining nine letters.
explanation.definitionFit: An abstainer refuses something offered, typically alcohol or a vote, so is someone who says no.

clue.text: Waiter tense with porter not opening

indicators.note: without its opening means the first letter is dropped

blocks.note: T is the grammatical abbreviation for tense
a porter carries luggage

explanation.surface: A nervous waiter stands beside a hotel porter who will not open the door.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Waiter' suggests restaurant staff but means one who waits: someone who tarries.
explanation.definitionFit: To tarry is to linger or delay, so a tarrier is someone who hangs about waiting.

clue.text: Almost complete relief to hold onto old vehicle

indicators.note: almost complete means one short of finished, so the last letter goes
holding onto something means clasping it inside your grip

blocks.note: charity is relief given to the poor
O is the standard abbreviation for old

explanation.surface: A sense of nearly total relief at being allowed to keep an old car.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Relief' reads as a feeling but is aid for the poor; CHARIT(Y) wraps round O.
explanation.definitionFit: A chariot is a two-wheeled horse-drawn carriage used in ancient warfare and racing.

clue.text: Search at high-street store for military apparel

blocks.note: to comb an area is to search it thoroughly
taken as written
Boots is a chain of chemists found on every British high street

explanation.surface: Someone hunts round a shop in town for army surplus clothing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Store' is not any shop but a named one: BOOTS, the British pharmacy chain.
explanation.definitionFit: Combat boots are sturdy laced boots issued to soldiers, part of their uniform or kit.

clue.text: Those desirous when king’s brought forward splendours

indicators.note: bringing something forward moves it earlier in the line, so one letter jumps ahead of its neighbour

blocks.note: people who lust are those desirous
R for rex, Latin for king

explanation.surface: Courtiers hungry for favour, as the king is ushered forward in all his splendour.
explanation.walkthrough: In LUSTERS the R moves one place earlier, in front of the E, to give LUSTRES.
explanation.definitionFit: Lustre means brilliance or glory, so lustres in the plural are splendours, radiant qualities.

clue.text: Management worry over difficulty losing leader

indicators.note: losing its leader means the word drops the letter at its head

blocks.note: to be in a stew is to be anxious
hardship is difficulty or suffering

explanation.surface: Bosses fretting about trouble after their chief has gone.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'over' places STEW above (H)ARDSHIP.
explanation.definitionFit: Stewardship is the careful running or supervision of something on behalf of others.

clue.text: Right Reverend invested with such power could be ideal guy

indicators.note: the answer, once it is invested with letters, makes a longer phrase, so taking those letters back out returns the answer

blocks.note: Mr Right is the perfect partner
RR is the abbreviation for Right Reverend, a bishop's title

explanation.surface: A bishop given such power might be the perfect man.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue works backwards: 'such' points to the answer, and the bishop's initials placed inside it make MR RIGHT, the ideal partner.
explanation.definitionFit: Might is strength or force, a synonym for power, as in the phrase might is right.

clue.text: Recalled gentle one admitted to disliking rock

indicators.note: recalling means calling back, so the word runs back the other way
being admitted to a place means being let in, so these letters go inside

blocks.note: tame means gentle and docile
I is the Roman numeral for one
hate means strong dislike

explanation.surface: Someone remembers a gentle soul who admitted disliking rock music.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rock' looks like music but is literal stone, and 'disliking' stands for the noun of strong aversion rather than a verb form.
explanation.definitionFit: Haematite is a reddish iron-ore mineral, the principal source of iron, found as rock.

clue.text: Heard an opponent coming

indicators.note: what is heard is taken by ear, so the sound matters rather than the spelling

blocks.note: a rival is an opponent

explanation.surface: Someone hears a competitor approaching.
explanation.walkthrough: Spoken quickly, A RIVAL is indistinguishable from ARRIVAL.
explanation.definitionFit: An arrival is the act of coming to a place, so the noun 'coming' is a synonym.

clue.text: Mean to collect unwrapped part that’s second-hand

indicators.note: collecting something means gathering it in, so one piece goes inside
unwrapping strips off the outer layer, so the outside letters go

blocks.note: mean in the sense of nasty
taken as written

explanation.surface: A miser picking up a used bit for free.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mean' looks like stingy or intend, but here it is VICIOUS, which takes in (P)AR(T).
explanation.definitionFit: Vicarious experience is felt through another person rather than directly, so it comes second-hand.

clue.text: Squealed feeling returned punch

indicators.note: something returned goes back the way it came, so the letters run backwards

blocks.note: to sing is slang for informing, as is to squeal
an air is a feeling or impression, as in an air of menace

explanation.surface: An informer squealed, and the sense of betrayal came back as a blow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Punch' reads as a blow but is the drink. 'Squealed' and SANG are both slang for informing to the police.
explanation.definitionFit: Sangria is a Spanish wine punch made with chopped fruit, so it is one kind of punch.

clue.text: People possessing cool garments

indicators.note: possessing means having or holding, so one piece is held within the other

blocks.note: bods is informal British slang for people
to ice is to cool

explanation.surface: Folk who own trendy clothes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cool' looks like trendy, but it is ICE, chilling something.
explanation.definitionFit: A bodice is the close-fitting upper part of a woman's dress, worn as an item of clothing.

clue.text: First person blocking thief is comparatively foolish

indicators.note: something blocking a passage sits inside it, stopping it up

blocks.note: a dipper is slang for a pickpocket
I is the first person pronoun

explanation.surface: The person who first stops a robber is acting rather daftly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'First person' sounds like whoever got there first, but it is the grammatical first person, I.
explanation.definitionFit: Dippy is informal for silly or scatterbrained, and dippier is its comparative form.

clue.text: Deeply emotive performing fabulously, withdrawing by back of Astoria

indicators.note: the back of a word is its final letter
withdrawing means pulling out, so these letters are taken away
performing is acting out, so the letters put on a new show in a different order

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written
last letter of Astoria

explanation.surface: A singer gives a moving, fabulous show before leaving the Astoria, a London music venue.
explanation.walkthrough: From FABULOUSLY take B, Y and A, then rearrange FULOUSL.
explanation.definitionFit: Soulful describes music or expression full of deep feeling, so it is a synonym for deeply emotive.

clue.text: Having bands start to practise in cleared-out shed

indicators.note: the start of a word is its opening letter
shedding means casting off, so that letter is lost

blocks.note: a room stripped of everything has been cleared out
first letter of practise

explanation.surface: Pop groups begin rehearsing in an emptied garden shed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shed' looks like a hut, but it is a verb: STRIPPED sheds the P that is 'in' it, losing one of its two Ps.
explanation.definitionFit: Something striped is marked with stripes, which are long bands of colour.

clue.text: Musician‘s followers endlessly travelled

indicators.note: without an end means the final letter is cut

blocks.note: sheep are people who follow the crowd unthinkingly
ran as in a train ran or travelled

explanation.surface: A singer's fans endlessly travel to see him on tour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Followers' suggests fans, but it is SHEEP, trimmed to SHEE.
explanation.definitionFit: Ed Sheeran is a hugely successful English singer-songwriter, so he is an example of a musician.

clue.text: Casual criticism of corporation’s passionate

blocks.note: corporation is old humorous slang for a pot belly, and the apostrophe S is kept
hot means passionate or ardent

explanation.surface: Offhand disapproval of a company's fervent attitude.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Corporation' looks like a company, but it is jokey British slang for a paunch, a pot.
explanation.definitionFit: A potshot is a random, unaimed remark of criticism, from firing a shot at whatever is in range.

clue.text: Timely drink after work with a Parisian

indicators.note: coming after means following, so one piece is placed behind the other

blocks.note: OP for opus, Latin for a work
port is a fortified wine
une is French for a, used with feminine nouns

explanation.surface: A well-timed drink after the office, with a person from Paris.
explanation.walkthrough: OP is the abbreviation for opus, a musical work; 'Parisian' signals a French word.
explanation.definitionFit: Opportune means happening at a convenient or suitable moment, which is the sense of well-timed.

clue.text: Dressing chef’s starter course involves

indicators.note: the starter of a word is its opening letter
to involve is to wrap up or include, so one piece goes inside another

blocks.note: a path is a course or route
first letter of chef

explanation.surface: A chef's opening course includes a salad dressing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dressing' and 'starter course' set up a menu, but the dressing is for a wound.
explanation.definitionFit: A patch is a pad or covering placed over a wound or eye, which is a kind of dressing.

clue.text: Not in step with partners? On the contrary

blocks.note: pas is a dance step, from French
in bridge, South and East are opponents, the contrary of partners

explanation.surface: A dancer is out of time with the other couples on the floor.
explanation.walkthrough: In bridge North-South and East-West are the partnerships, so S and E are opponents; 'on the contrary' turns 'partners' into that pair.
explanation.definitionFit: Passé means out of fashion, and something not in fashion is described as simply not in.

clue.text: Incident from knocking back drams not pleasant

definitions.note: incident is used as an adjective: arising from

indicators.note: knocking something back pushes it the opposite way, so the letters run backwards

blocks.note: a nip is a small measure of spirits
food that is off is unpleasant

explanation.surface: An unpleasant episode that came of downing whisky.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Knocking back' tempts you to read drinking; here it reverses NIPS.
explanation.definitionFit: A spin-off is a by-product or secondary result that arises incidentally from something larger.

clue.text: Fruit in rank drink reportedly

indicators.note: what is reported is passed on by word of mouth, so the sound is used rather than the spelling

blocks.note: a row is a rank or line
to sip is to drink in small amounts

explanation.surface: Some fruit in a foul-tasting drink, apparently.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rank' looks like foul but is a row; said quickly, ROWS SIP runs together like ROSE-HIP.
explanation.definitionFit: The rosehip is the red seed-pod fruit of the rose bush, used for syrup and tea.

clue.text: Brilliant present ordered with loan acquired

indicators.note: putting things in order rearranges them, so the letters are sorted anew
what is acquired is taken in, so one piece ends up inside the other

blocks.note: taken as written
lend means to loan

explanation.surface: A dazzling gift bought on credit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Loan' is the verb lend; it sits inside RESPENT, an arrangement of PRESENT.
explanation.definitionFit: Resplendent means dazzlingly impressive in appearance, so it is a synonym of brilliant.
